title: Hunting playbook (one per canonical bug class)
description: A playbook is the framework's PRIOR for one bug class: what invariants to extract, how a claim decomposes into assumptions (templates the proposer instantiates per target), the prioritized hunt order, how attempts at this class typically die, and the prior rejections most likely to be re-raised. It is context for the proposer — never a verdict, never an instruction to the orchestrator. Every tool id must exist in the tool registry (sandbox profiles + analysis tools).

bug_class.description: the canonical class (taxonomy.known_classes) this playbook serves

description.description: what this class attacks and what a genuine instance looks like

evidence_floor.description: informational: the class's default CONFIRMED floor; the campaign's floor policy governs

investigation_mode.description: how this class is hunted: code-reading (default; legacy playbooks omit it) or adversarial-simulation — game-theoretic multi-actor modeling, requires the simulation block

action_space.description: the moves available to the cast: entry points plus off-path actions (direct transfers, mempool timing)

ordering_freedoms.description: which orders of the cast's moves are free (cross-tx / intra-block) and which are fixed

expectation_violated.description: invariant-id reference into this playbook's invariants list — the documented expectation the strategy profile violates; a reference cannot drift from the statement it names

simulation.description: the game-theoretic prior for adversarial-simulation playbooks: the cast with behavior classes, action space, ordering freedoms, and the violated expectation as an invariant-id reference

typical_documentation.description: where protocols usually document this property (README anchor, NatSpec convention)

assumption_templates.description: the decomposition skeleton the proposer instantiates per target; {placeholders} mark target-specific values

preferred_tools.description: must come from the tool registry

hunt_order.description: the prioritized investigation sequence — cheap falsification first

stop_if.description: the observation that kills this hypothesis early

failure_modes.description: how attempts at this class typically fail or die — the cheapest lessons available

typical_rejection_class.description: which rejection class this failure mode most often produces

negative_memory_hooks.description: the prior rejections most likely to be re-raised for this class, and the proposition each turned on — pre-filled so the proposer can override with a materially different hypothesis

exploit_shape.description: the canonical economic/technical shape of an instance of this class

amplifiers.description: risk-multiplier primitives that make an instance of this class pay more; pre-screen metadata, never evidence
